quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are far enough away from the vehicle you passed. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
They brake more slowly than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop very quickly. Following too closely puts your life and the motorcyclist's life in danger. You need enough time and space to stop if the motorcyclist makes a sudden move or stop.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning while driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed that is normal for dry conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires lose contact with the road. Your vehicle will slide on top of the water. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent it is to drive slower in rain or wet conditions than you would in dry weather.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars disappear into the truck's blind spots. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Driving in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare in one direction while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often. This helps you know where vehicles are around you.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means "stop." You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts is FALSE?

options.text: They keep you in place during a crash.
They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.
They keep you from being thrown from the vehicle in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.
questions.explanation: State law requires you to wear seat belts even if your vehicle has airbags. Airbags protect you from hitting the steering wheel, dashboard, and windshield. However, they do not protect you in side crashes, rear crashes, or rollovers. Seat belts are always necessary.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual location, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked vehicle should not be a hazard to other drivers. Park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the roadway while driving?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may jump or change direction suddenly. Animals often travel in groups, so there may be more animals you cannot see that are also near the road.

questions.question: What is the law about alcohol in a vehicle on a highway?

options.text: You cannot drink from or have open containers of alcohol in a vehicle.
Passengers can drink alcohol if the driver is not drinking.
The driver can drink alcohol if they are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drink from or have open containers of alcohol in a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. Neither drivers nor passengers may drink alcohol or have open containers of alcohol in a vehicle while it is being driven.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Children on bikes may ride on the sidewalk and suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Press the brakes hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, keep the wheel steady, and let the car slow down naturally.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Push yourself to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, pull over at a rest stop to take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest and can make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does an orange and red triangle on a vehicle mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and horse-drawn carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when entering a freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What is a result of driving too fast?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It improves your ability to react.
It leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often causes drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Down the middle between them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between them.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right, steer between them. This gives you the most space on both sides.

questions.question: How does speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Faster speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. Higher speeds increase the risk of serious injury and death. Leave more space between cars as you drive faster.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after stopping.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal before turning.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Everyone can pass.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line, only the driver next to the dashed line can cross it to pass. The driver next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: Which statement about drinking and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal limit, driving is safe.
Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol hurts your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react quickly and safely while driving. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When there is a solid yellow line on your side, passing is not allowed. Sometimes both sides have solid yellow lines, meaning no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires float on water instead of touching the road. How do you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep the same speed.
Drive slower.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: In rain, drive slower to prevent hydroplaning. If you drive too fast, your tires can float on water and lose contact with the road. This makes your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles, so you need more room to stop if the rider brakes suddenly. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.
